items.title: Lanterns: Who Killed Hal Jordan and More of Our Biggest Questions Heading Into the Finale
items.excerpt: Who killed Hal Jordan? Is Hal Jordan even dead!? What's up with Sinestro and that planet? We have so many questions heading into the Lanterns season finale...
items.content_text: Spoilers follow for Lanterns Episodes 1-7. Lanterns, am I right? While the HBO series set in James Gunn’s DC Universe was divisive among some fans at the outset – what with the whole killing off Hal Jordan in the first episode situation – it has become increasingly buzzy with each passing week, with showrunner Chris Mundy and his fellow creators Damon Lindelof and Tom King building mystery upon mystery over the course of the first season. And now, as we head into the season finale this weekend, there are a ton of questions that need to be answered. We’re breaking down the biggest ones we have right here, but please comment below and let us know what other questions you might have regarding Lanterns Season 1… and the possible answers and theories you have as well! Who Killed Hal Jordan? Assuming, of course, Hal (Kyle Chandler) even is dead (see below for more on that), there are obviously several possibilities as to who could’ve put a bullet in the ex-Green Lantern’s head in the 2026 time period. The chief suspects seem to be: John Stewart Sheriff Kerry Kane Noah Macon Hal himself John Stewart Taking these one at a time, it seems pretty unlikely that John (Aaron Pierre) would’ve killed Hal. For starters, he’s one of our two lead characters, and while both of these Lanterns can be sort of assholes – especially to each other – they’re still ultimately meant to be figures who we sympathize with and want to cheer on. But even beyond that, it doesn’t make much story sense for John to have done this; he essentially already “beat” Hal during the events of Episode 5 , leaving him a broken man without the ring and only the consequences of his own actions left to face up to. By the time we catch up with John, now an architect and businessman, in 2026, he clearly still harbors a lot of feelings about his past as a Lantern, but needing to kill Hal is not one of them. Sheriff Kerry Kane Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) on the other hand, well… as much as we love her, the good sheriff has been known to keep secrets from our heroes in the past. And while I buy that she and the post-prison, repentant Hal had a thing going, as well as that she is truly gutted by his death, that doesn’t mean that their relationship would’ve kept her from doing the deed if it was necessary for a greater cause. Let’s not forget, Kerry was saved by Zoe Macon the Manhunter (Poorna Jagannathan) back when she first arrived in Rushville while on the run from Gotham City. And it was during that encounter that she essentially swore her allegiance to Zoe. So if there is still some contingency plan in place for Zoe, even though John killed the Manhunter in 2016, there’s every reason to believe that Kerry would still be instrumental in keeping that plan on track… Noah Macon Which brings us to Kerry’s son, Noah (Shea Pritchard). There sure seems to be something fishy with this kid – the dude went and copped out on the college hat ceremony after the whole town showed up for it with bated breath! He also, you know, had a grandmother (step-grandmother, but still) who was a Manhunter. We’ll talk more about him below, but he’s high on the list of suspects. Hal Himself Look, Kerry told John how, after he got out of prison, Hal was on a relentless mission in Rushville to make up for the disastrous events that landed him behind bars in the first place, knocking on doors and offering his help and such. Is it out of the realm of possibility to think that in order to keep the town safe this time – or maybe even to make up for what happened to the town 10 years ago in 2016 – that he would take his own life if need be? That is, assuming he actually did die… Wait, But Is Hal Really Dead? I’ve already talked about this before , but it’s very much not out of the realm of possibility that Hal isn’t even dead. Maybe he’s just “dead-ish” even? We already know that the show is full of aliens who walk around posing as humans, which means that the body we’ve seen could just be an alien that took Hal’s form. It’s also possible that Hal is regenerating from the wounds that killed him. Yes, it’s a crazy sci-fi concept, but John previously got a total skin graft after Zoe let him burn in that car fire and, as many eagle-eyed fans have pointed out, the trailer for the season finale shows a similar circular mark on Hal’s inner arm that John had after that Manhunter Miracle Medicine. Zoe explained to John that basically her tech required a skin sample (pulled from that spot on his arm) in order to repair/replace his burned skin, so perhaps the same methodology is being used to fix Hal… albeit it would have to unscramble his shot-up brains in this case. Or maybe the dead body was just a clone spawned from that same technology? Why Can John Stewart Create Constructs Without the Ring? Remember in Episode 2 when John tried to fly, but instead he created a cute little green bird construct? And the bird still existed and followed him around, even when he didn’t have the ring on? This was the first – but not last – indication that John has some kind of, well, super superpower that other Green Lanterns don’t. The Halogram is very impressed by this ability in Episode 7 , when John summons him without the ring, saying “Bravo… it’s goddamned incredible!” It’s nice to get compliments from your seemingly dead mentor’s hologram. 'Bravo… it’s goddamned incredible!' -The Halogram But that still doesn’t answer how he’s able to do it. Presumably, John’s extraordinary ability to Green Lantern without a Green Lantern ring is tied to his extreme potential and the frankly insane training during his childhood by his we-need-a-new-word-for-helicopter-parents parents. Don’t forget, Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) told Hal from Space Azkaban that the second greatest threat Hal was facing was the Manhunter, with the implication being that the greatest threat was John. And what could be more powerful than a Green Lantern who doesn’t need the ring… or the Guardians for that matter? Is Noah Macon Part Manhunter? Again, this perfect Rushville all-state quarterback has got to have something going on beyond being a perfect Rushville all-state quarterback. The hat ceremony thing, which I previously mentioned, was just weird (and also rude), but also, with such a short season, why would the show’s writers introduce the aged-up version of Noah in Episode 6 if he wasn’t going to be important in some way? In Episode 5, his step-grandmother/Manhunter Zoe tells the young Noah (Cary Christopher) to remember what she taught him… and that’s the same episode where everything goes to hell in a handbasket in town. We know Zoe meticulously planned her own protection by essentially drafting half the town to work for her, including Noah’s mom, so it only makes sense that she would have Tony Soprano/Batman-style contingency plans upon plans upon plans, including what would happen if she was killed. But then again, are we sure it was even Zoe who actually died in Episode 5? Could Noah be Zoe!? What’s the Deal With Sinestro on That Dead Planet? Man, speaking of really holding your fire until the end of a short season. Sinestro, discussed here or there and seen briefly in Episodes 2 and 4, finally shows up at the end of Episode 7, seemingly stranded on the dead world that John and the Halogram have traveled to via portal… but apparently meant to be an important part of the season finale. Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) had previously said that someone broke Sinestro out of the Guardians’ prison, and that Hal was a likely suspect if not for the fact that he was also in (Earth) prison. (And by the way, the timeline here is a little wonky because Guy tells John this info in an almost whispery, gossipy way, as if it’s breaking news, but meanwhile we know Hal has been out of prison for about a year – and is believed to be dead – at that point. Which would mean Sinestro must’ve broken out of Space Azkaban at least a year ago.) So how does Sinestro popping up on that alien planet connect to everything? This is the same world that Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor) and his people hailed from, a race that was virtually wiped out by the Manhunters. It’s also the world that Hal left a portal to in his storage unit, which he apparently wanted John to find. Did Hal want Sinestro and John to team up for some reason? Neither is a particular fan of the Guardians, so could Hal perhaps be orchestrating some kind of Oan revolution from beyond the grave… one last “f you” to the powers that be? What Did Kerry Get Up to in Gotham That Was So Bad? We saw in flashback how Kerry would’ve been killed by a pair of scary dudes who had tracked her from Gotham City to Rushville, if not for the timely intervention of Zoe. After being saved by Zoe, she essentially began a new life in the town and eventually became sheriff (and a secret surrogate of Zoe’s). As IGN’s Jesse Schedeen has previously pointed out, Kerry’s name is also a big Batman clue : the Kane family are related to Bruce Wayne, as Martha Wayne was originally Martha Kane. Kathy Kane and Kate Kane, depending on when you were reading comics or watching CW shows, were both also Batwoman. So assuming the name of this character is not an accident – and not much on this show is – we’ve gotta wonder how a high-falutin’ member of the Kane family could fall in with such a rough element that she would’ve been killed if not for a Manhunter. It seems unlikely that Lanterns Season 1 will have time to dig further into this topic, but if the show moves forward with a Season 2, perhaps we’ll learn more about Kerry’s history… and maybe even any rich, famous, orphaned, dressed-in-black cousins she might have back home? Remind Me: What Exactly Has Been the Order of Succession for Earth’s Green Lanterns? This one’s easy! In 1986, Abin Sur crashed on Earth, and his ring almost went to John Stewart’s father, but Stewart Sr. couldn’t cut it, so instead Hal Jordan inherited the Green Lantern mantle. Hal was Earth’s Lantern for the next 20 years, until the disaster in Rushville when John took the ring from him. But he rejected the Guardians’ offer to become the new Green Lantern. It was around this same time that the gym teacher named Guy Gardner became the new Green Lantern, and continues to be through 2026. (Also, for comics fans, it seems that Alan Scott – the Golden Age Green Lantern – never took the mantle… in this timeline anyway.) What questions do you have heading into the Lanterns finale? Let’s discuss below!

items.title: Vibe-Coded Mashup Mods Have Taken Over X This Week
items.excerpt: I have spent the last three days scrolling through some of the most insane mod videos I've ever seen. Modders are taking games that have been decompiled with Claude, and mashing them up with other games. As the week has gone on, there have only been more clips of these mods pouring out on X/Twitter.
items.content_text: I have spent the last three days scrolling through some of the most insane mod videos I've ever seen. Modders are taking games that have been decompiled with Claude, and mashing them up with other games. As the week has gone on, there have only been more clips of these mods pouring out on X/Twitter. One person created a mashup of World of Warcraft and Call of Duty: World at War ; another combined Escape From Tarkov with Skyrim . There’s even one that takes Insomniac’s Spider-Man and combines it with Batman Arkham City , where the player is able to swing around Batman’s turf. These mods are everywhere online right now, though they thankfully haven’t filtered into modding websites like Nexus Mods yet. But, with the sheer volume of these mods and with how accessible Opus 5.5 is, it feels like it’s only a matter of time before the gates are fully torn down. And if that happens, it could change the face of the modding scene entirely. Why Now? Claude Opus 5.5 launched last week, promising cheaper tokens and more efficient code work. I'm sure that Anthropic meant for it to be used by professionals, but gamers have used it to create some of the weirdest mods I have ever seen. Opus is a model that can power AI agents, which can be deployed to create entire games from the engine, to the art and enemy behavior. Brendan Jowett has a great video on YouTube of the model in action: He develops little slices of video games and compares them directly with the same tasks from OpenAI’s Astra 6 model. While the results of both are far from what you’d expect from a fully featured game, Claude’s new model has clearly come a long way. The problem with the examples in Jowett’s video is that while the models are good at piecing together disparate parts of a game, enemy AI (lol) and art assets are lackluster to say the least. In one of the slices, a space combat sim, the space fighter flys at a diagonal angle, while moving in a straight line ahead, and shooting. In another slice enemies completely ignore the player character. As good as Claude Opus 5.5 seems to be, it’s still lightyears away from developing something like a true mashup of Minecraft and Elden Ring from scratch. But the model doesn’t have to start from scratch. The big, driving force behind a lot of these mods is decompilation, where people are pointing Opus at a game and letting the agent break it down to its source code (here’s a handy blog if you want to really get in the weeds). Just earlier today, we covered Halo: Combat Evolved being decompiled and ported to run natively in a browser . Once that step is complete, it takes little effort to take that source code and work huge swaths of games into other games as mods, and with very little input from the user. Couple that with the relatively affordable tokens, and it shouldn’t be surprising that X/Twitter’s generally pro-AI users went wild with it, creating hundreds of mashups. And it doesn’t seem like it’s slowing down any time soon; what started off as a weird video that my boss sent me on Tuesday has now evolved to the point where I can’t even open X/Twitter without seeing a deluge of these mods. Piracy? The obvious problem with all of this is that these models are breaking open games developed by real people, getting the source code and then just mashing stuff together without consideration or permission from the original developers. That’s nothing particularly new – the modding scene is definitely no stranger to mashups, all the Thomas the Tank Engine mods are proof of that. However, this trend might be breaking into new territory, thanks to decompilation. This could be another reason none of these mods have made their way onto any distribution platforms. Nexus Mods doesn’t outright ban AI-generated content, but it doesn’t let people use AI tools to upload content that they don’t have the rights to. In a blog post from 2023, Nexus laid out its rules around AI generated content. The policy states that , “In order to prevent any issues with your mods, we encourage you to avoid using these tools unless you have explicit permission to use all the assets. This is particularly true for AI-generated voice acting but also covers images, models, code and anything else that you can use this technology to create.” Every single one of these passthrough mods are using images, models, and code that the people generating them don’t have the rights to. But it’s only a matter of time until some platform holder allows these mods to be hosted, and I’m sure a massive legal battle will happen immediately afterwards. The Modding Community Hates This Way before all of these Claude-authored mod videos started cropping up online, people had been creating mods by hand for years, typically out of pure love for the game. It shouldn’t be surprising, then, that a lot of mod authors aren’t fans of this phenomenon. Mod authors have been expressing their frustration on X/Twitter as this has been happening. “I mod games and I'm not shy about the fact that I use AI to do it. I hate this bullshit ‘trend’. Pure slop, there's nothing creative about this at all,” kran27_ posted. “AI has a lot of potential in the modding scene, but the shit that's getting the clicks is this jingling keys bullshit.” Kran wasn’t alone, with discountmodder ready to just leave the scene, saying, “Dude I'm really disappointed. If this becomes the permanent state of modding, this may be my last project. I don't wanna be involved in an AI slop-factory.” I can’t escape the feeling that most of these mashups are born from people just playing with a new AI model and seeing what will happen, and I hope that this weird trend will die off soon. Modding is one of the best parts of PC gaming, and there is a lot of incredible content that people make just because they love a game. Some of the best games started off as mods, after all, and without them we never would have got the likes of Half-Life or League of Legends. I hope that this is just a trend, rather than a sign of where the modding scene is heading. Fortunately, because these mods seemingly only exist to farm engagement on Twitter (at least so far), you don’t have to worry too much about them if you just want to start a new modded run of The Witcher 3 Remastered. If anything, it just means that if you want to avoid AI content, you need to pay even more attention to who you’re getting your mods from.

items.title: Verity Review
items.excerpt: Verity review: A veritable mess starring Anne Hathaway, Dakota Johnson, and Josh Hartnett.
items.content_text: Verity is in theaters now. In a Guardian piece on how Colleen Hoover became a global best-selling author, one YA fan that was interviewed by the paper suggested it was because she’s “writing for people who don’t like reading.” If that's the case, then one could argue that the film adaptations of her work are for people who don't like cinema. Now that I've watched all four films inspired by her literary prose — 2024's It Ends with Us, 2025's Regretting You, this year's Reminders of Him, and now Verity — I'm making that case. For these are not adaptations that make any attempt to elevate the middling narratives fumbling around Hoover's novels; I realised this when reading It Ends with Us after suffering through the movie, and I vowed never to read another. With Verity, I had more hope that it would buck the trend. Divorced from the sentimentality of previous adaptations, this story opens with a meet-cute that’ll give you whiplash. After introducing Anne Hathaway's best-selling author Verity Crawford through interviews with the likes of Gayle King, where she discusses the darkness in her writing, struggling writer Lowen Ashleigh (Dakota Johnson) enters the chat. Lowen's agent has landed her a meeting with Crawford's publishing house for a mysterious job opportunity, but on the way, she not only witnesses a road accident but is drenched in the blood of the cyclist involved. It's an opener as out there as the one in Meet Joe Black (IYKYK), but it does provide an opportunity for Josh Hartnett's handsome stranger to step in and help clean her up. In typical Hoover fashion, the pair trauma bond: He tells her he dragged his dead daughter out of a lake, and she says her mother died of cancer the week before. There’s no build up, just some awkward exposition-dumping in a men's toilet. They're soon reunited at the publishing house, where it’s revealed that he's Verity's husband, Jeremy. He and the editors want to commission Lowen to finish his wife's novel series; Verity is in a comatose state after a car accident and cannot speak or move. So, with little deliberation and due to the shoehorned fact that Lowen is also being evicted from her New York apartment, she packs up and moves into the Crawfords' sprawling Vermont home for six months. There she meets Verity, a shell of her glamorous self wearing a glazed stare. This is one of the few scenes the women share; most of Hathaway's performance is marginalised to interviews on the likes of Hot Ones and the Call Her Daddy podcast, as well as flashbacks layered with sultry voiceovers as Lowen reads Verity's secret autobiography. Every time she picks it up, sentences run across the screen, and often Lowen is superimposed over scenes from the past to try to enliven the act of reading. It doesn't. What's most infuriating is how long it takes Lowen to finish the text. It’s unbelievable that an author would constantly run away from the autobiography to masturbate and go on a date with Jeremy, given how unflinching Verity's candour is. She reveals juicy details about her marriage and hints that their daughter's death might not have been an accident — how did she not finish it in one sitting? Nothing screams “padding for time” more than this tedious set-up, accomplishing little in the way of ingratiating the viewer with Johnson's "pick me" girl protagonist. Nothing screams “padding for time” more than this tedious set-up. Nor does it scratch the surface of who Jeremy actually is beyond the one-dimensional trope of a swoon-worthy husband. Screenwriter Nick Antosca, who recently impressed with his adaptation of Cape Fear, hints at some resentment on Jeremy’s part for his wife's success, but the script never probes deeper than in a final act reveal that flings the missing pieces at you in one blink. The best Antosca offers is an examination of the reliability of the narrator, but even that effort is phoned in. Michael Showalter's direction is similarly dull, conveying little of the vision seen in his Oscar-nominated films, The Eyes of Tammy Faye and The Big Sick. Instead, it plods an uneven, uninspiring route into cliché and lazy convention. That Anne Hathaway has been on an exquisite run of big screen releases from The Odyssey and Mother Mary to The End of Oak Street and The Devil Wears Prada 2 makes this, her last 2026 performance, even more disappointing. What a lead balloon for everyone involved — one that proves a moratorium on Colleen Hoover adaptations is long overdue. To misquote Lady Catherine from Pride and Prejudice: "Are the shades of cinema to be thus polluted?"

items.content_text: Walmart exclusively has the best price on Switch 2 memory cards. The Onn 512GB MicroSD Express Memory Card is in stock for $84.77 and the 256GB model is also in stock for $46.77, both with free shipping. Better yet, there's a new unadvertised coupon code " SAVE3X " that takes an additional $10 off either memory card! That brings the prices down to $74.77 and $36.77 , respectively. Your mileage may vary (it might not work for you) but we've confirmed that it is working for a lot of people. items.title: Amazon Is Dropping Prices on Green Lantern Merch Ahead of Lanterns Season Finale
items.content_text: DC's latest live action series is wrapping up its first season this weekend. Even if the series makes some interesting departures from the source material, it's safe to say that Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart have charmed both new and existing fans of the Green Lantern. Amazon happens to be launching its October Prime Day sale next week. In the lead-up to that sale and the Lanterns season finale, the retailer has dropped prices on tons of Green Lantern merch. If you’ve fallen for the space cops or are just looking for an easy Halloween costume, now’s a great time to grab some gear. Green Lantern Merch Sale Ahead of Lanterns Season Finale Note: Most of these deals are exclusive to Prime members . You can sign up for a 30-day free trial here . There’s not an easy sale hub to scroll through, so I’ve just picked out all of the officially licensed Green Lantern merch I could find on sale. You’ll find 15% discounts across the board, which might not seem like much, but is most likely the best price we’ll see on these shirts, which typically stick at $20, all year. Two of the shirts on sale are specifically based on the new Lanterns series, showing images of Aaron Pierre and Kyle Chandler in their respective roles. Like the rest of the sale, these are officially licensed shirts straight from DC Comics. Other shirts are based on specific comic versions of the same characters. One of my personal favorites shows a comic cover of Jordan with the quote “Hal Yeah.” Suits him, you know. Even more shirts take a simplistic approach to the overarching Green Lantern iconography. You have plenty of options with the Green Lantern logo, or a graphic print of the full Green Lantern oath. Some shirts even feature full panels from various comic runs. While they aren't included in Amazon's deals, Funko Pop is dropping a new line of Green Lantern figures at NYCC. An official Lanterns Power Ring is also available for $70 through the official DC Shop . Green Lantern Comics Also on Sale Amazon has also been discounting a spread of Green Lantern comics. These deals have nothing to do with Prime Day, so you don't have to be a Prime member to grab them. The best discounts are on the omnibus editions of the iconic run by Geoff Johns, which resurrected the one and only Hal Jordan. As for Lanterns itself, writer announcements would suggest a second season is at the very least in development. We still have a truckload of questions going into the season finale, including how our beloved Lanterns might fit into the ( now Paramount-owned ) future of the DCU .

items.title: Ex-Rockstar Boss Dan Houser Doesn't Play a Lot of Open-World Games – and Doesn't Plan to Play GTA 6
items.excerpt: Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.
items.content_text: Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures. "Given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he told Variety . I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently." "It’s not my job within any company that I’ve ever worked at, thankfully, to be the person that understands what everyone else is doing," Houser continued. "I’m trying to think about new ways of doing it. So when we worked on Red Dead Redemption, as soon as we started working, I never watched another Western. I never watched The Sopranos until after I left Rockstar. I saw one episode, because my girlfriend-now-wife and I did watch the finale in real time. I’d not seen any of it before that moment. And then I watched it all during COVID. And I’m grateful. It’s so good that it would have disrupted everything I did on GTA, had I watched at the time. So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me." "I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me." On not playing many other open-world games, Houser said, "I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature.’ I’m not a game designer, I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about." Houser's new company, Absurd Ventures, is currently working on two games, as discussed in my all-too-brief conversation with him at LA Comic-Con last year. The studio has already released American Caper, a graphic novel series. Its double-sized season-finale issue drops next month – a week before GTA 6 – along with the book "A Better Paradise."

items.title: GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms New Details on Sex, Drug Use, Decapitation, and More
items.excerpt: GTA 6 has received a rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.
items.content_text: UPDATE October 2, 2026, 11:39 a.m. PT: PEGI has seemingly updated its website to remove the age rating for GTA 6. The PEGI 18 page – which, as viewed by IGN, included what appeared to be new details about GTA 6 – is no longer available. In its place is a blank listing that says, "The requested page could not be found." Users on X/Twitter have captured and shared an image of the listing and have continued to share its contents across social media. IGN has reached out to PEGI for comment. Grand Theft Auto VI PEGI rating is now up! https://t.co/av3HXd6GQf pic.twitter.com/6MhVcAA1xc — iGrandTheftAuto.com (@iGrandTheftAuto) October 2, 2026 ORIGINAL STORY: GTA 6 has received an age rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more. The update, which can be found on the Pan European Game Information board's website , gives players a relatively in-depth description of Rockstar Games' megaton video game ahead of its launch in November. The PEGI 18 rating arrives just one day after GTA 6 received its official ESRB rating , which, also unsurprisingly, resulted in an "M for Mature." GTA 6's rating describes a story that allows players to take control of "Jason Duval or Lucia Caminos, two criminals who become involved in a criminal conspiracy following a failed robbery." It adds that they'll work together as "they become increasingly entangled in criminal activities" in Vice City, with gameplay that, as we've already seen, is par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto. What's different about GTA 6 is the unprecedented detail Rockstar has shoved into the game , with previous footage showing off an open-world sandbox with enough activities to make up for the 13-year wait. PEGI dived into that, too, but there are still even more new highlights to go over. The board described the game's violence as "bloody with a high degree of realism." Some weapons will be more brutal than others, with some said to be "able to cause greater damage, such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." This time around, Rockstar has made drug use "frequent and prominent," with players able to partake in illicit substances. Cocaine is said to be especially important in Vice City, with the rating promising that Jason and Lucia will be able to use the substance directly from their inventory, as it can be "snorted directly from their hand at any time." The GTA 6 PEGI description also touched on " strong sexual themes ," which include "nudity, scenes of intercourse, and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." It's a lot that we knew and some details that we didn't, but you can read the "content specific issues" section of the summary in its entirety below. "This game contains frequent depictions of violence; due to the free roam nature of the game the player can harm all other characters inhabiting the environment," PEGI said. "This includes civilians, criminals and the authorities. Violence is bloody with a high degree of realism, with certain weapons being able to cause greater damage such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment. "Drug use is frequent and prominent with the player being able to partake in drug use with others and to use illegal drugs directly from their inventory. Most notably, cocaine can be carried around by the player and snorted directly from their hand at any time. "There are also strong sexual themes, including nudity, scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes. In various night clubs the player can also pay for private dances, during which, the game allows the player to move their hands onto the dancers’ breasts and buttocks." The PEGI age rating also mentioned "other issues," including that domestic animals can be harmed, though not in the same detail as humans. The word "f**k" is also featured prominently in the game, while the word "c**t" is only occasionally featured. The description also said that "discriminatory language can be heard in the TV shows and on the radio channels." Finally, GTA 6 reminds players that they will have the option to purchase in-game items, though it's still unclear what this entails. In August, it was reported that Rockstar would not include microtransactions or generative AI in the game . GTA 6 is still on course to launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. You can read more about how Rockstar has ramped up its marketing tactics here , and you can see what we learned from some new screenshots here . While we wait for any more updates, you can read IGN's interview and preview .

items.title: 4 Things to Focus on Outside Combat in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave
items.content_text: We’re back for a new installment in our The Long Game series, where we break down things you can invest in early in games that will pay off long-term. Today we’re focusing on Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, the huge new installment in the long-running series that takes you to the capital of the Dagdan Empire to be a gladiator in the Heroic Games. Like its predecessor Three Houses, Fortune’s Weave has a split narrative with multiple protagonists. However, this time around, you don’t have to choose one route. You can follow the stories of Cai, Leda, Dietrich, and Theodora in any order and can switch between them at any time once you reach Dagsion, the central hub city. As with the rest of the Fire Emblem series, Fortune’s Weave is centered on grid-based strategy combat. But it also features a heavy focus on activities outside of combat, with access to a world map you can traverse between story battles. You can find dungeons, towns, traveling merchants, and skirmishes with roving enemies. That’s on top of running around the giant city of Dagsion, which is full of shops, activities, and people to meet. It can all be a little overwhelming, especially if you’re new to the series and aren’t sure where to start. So that’s what we’re here to help with. Here are four things outside of combat that you can (and should) start taking advantage of as soon as you can. Show Your Support Support levels and conversations have long been a staple of the Fire Emblem series, with characters amassing points whenever they fight next to each other or provide healing or support in combat. Fortune’s Weave expands that system and adds new ways to build support outside of combat, which you should take advantage of whenever possible. The primary way of building support is by eating meals together at the inn, which will be available to all protagonists very early in the game. Three people can eat together at once, and everyone has their own food preferences. The inn menu changes daily, and when you pick your group of three, you can see how they feel about each meal. The amount of support points everyone gains is based on how much they like the meal, so don’t try to force people to eat stuff they don’t like. Meals are particularly helpful for building support points with people who aren’t actively in your party and are a vital way to convince recruits to join you (more on that in a bit), since you can’t build support with them in combat. You’ll eventually unlock arena training, where you can assign two fighters to train with each other in a variety of ways. This will boost both fighters’ command of weapons, magic, or movement types, while also giving them support points with each other. Arena training is the most valuable way to prepare characters for more advanced combat classes. Plus, it’s available every week, so don’t forget to come back to Dagsion every once in a while to take advantage of it. Raise Your Renown Each protagonist will learn about Renown once they get to Dagsion early in the game, and it’s basically a stat that measures how well known you are in the city. Increasing your Renown adds important boosts at certain thresholds, will make it possible to recruit more characters, and it’s a big part of the central gameplay loop of Fortune’s Weave. All protagonists can take on subquests given out by people throughout Dagsion, most of which will take you onto the world map to find items or get rid of certain enemies. These subquests each give Renown and all have deadlines, but they’re usually pretty forgiving, so you should have plenty of time to do them all. Paralogues are the exception to that standard. These are more significant side quests that expand on the stories of individual characters. Fire Emblem veterans will already be familiar with paralogues, but they're handled differently in Fortune's Weave than the rest of the series. You can only start one if you talk to the right character in Dagsion during a set period of time, and the deadlines for paralogues are strict (in the most extreme case, there's one on Dietrich's path you can only get on one specific date). This can be an issue because you might spend an extended period on the world map and blow right past the cutoff date without even realizing a paralogue was available. You won't receive any in-game notification, you just have to be in Dagsion on the correct dates. Completing a paralogue nets you 20,000 gold, a bunch of Renown, and unlocks recruitment for certain characters, so they're very worthwhile. I don't normally recommend playing with a guide, but this is one area where I think it's a good idea to look up the information beforehand. You need to be aware of the dates when paralogues are available so you can plan accordingly. Luckily, IGN has a full breakdown of their dates across all protagonists. You can also earn Renown by visiting gods in their temples in Dagsion. This becomes available early in the game, but it can be easy to forget about since you don’t get reminded about it. On the map, there are icons for each god’s temple. You might notice that on some days, one of those icons is yellow, which means that god is there in person and available to visit. If you continue chatting with the same god, they’ll get chummy with you and might reveal some additional information about themselves or lore about the world. While completing subquests and paralogues is the base way everyone can gain Renown, each protagonist also has an additional one that’s unique to them. Cai’s involves doing more quests, called kindness quests. Dietrich can summon enemies to battle at any time, as well as duel combatants in dungeons to steal their combat arts. Theodora gets resource requests that allow her to trade items you’ve gathered for Renown. And for Leda, remember to check the tavern in Dagsion at the start of each chapter. She’ll have new performance requests in certain cities on the world map, where she can dance to receive thousands of gold and hundreds of Renown at once. Mind Your Materials Character levels and class progression are obviously important in Fortune’s Weave, but don’t forget about their equipment. You’ll start with wooden weapons, but the armory will quickly add bronze and iron versions that are significantly more powerful. You should upgrade as soon as you’re able to. In Chapter 6, regardless of whose path you’re following, you’ll be introduced to the blacksmith. The main one is in Dagsion, but some bigger towns on the world map will have one too. They allow you to spend money and smithing materials to upgrade your weapons, with basic weapons only requiring Smithing Stones and more specialized equipment requiring unique materials. You can gather these materials on the world map, but the best places to find them are mines. These dungeons have crystal deposits you can smash that will earn you guaranteed smithing materials. As you’d expect, higher level mines will have more unique materials, and you can gather a bunch of them in one trip. Dungeons will also be filled with boxes and barrels you can smash with an attack, and ones that hold items will have golden sparkles on them. You can get a variety of materials this way, including stones and food. Food can be used at rest spots in dungeons or feast spots on the world map to restore your health and magic, which is particularly important when you’re planning on staying outside of town for a while. Some quests and recruits will also require particular vegetables, meat, or fish, so try to keep a variety of food items on hand in case you need them. If you’re playing as Cai, he can also use food as bait to lure out animals to catch and use as mounts. If you use rare food, noted by a blue icon with a sparkle in the corner, you’re more likely to attract rare animals. Just make sure you use the kind of food each animal likes: orniuses like fish, horses and pegasi prefer vegetables, while wild bau like meat. Rally Your Recruits No matter which protagonist you’re leading, your core group of characters won’t be enough to take on later chapters. You’ll need to add to your ranks by recruiting some of the many characters scattered around Dagsion, but you don’t have to wander aimlessly and hope you run into them. All characters will be noted by dots on the map: an orange dot marks a character you haven’t met yet, a green dot means you’ve spoken to them but haven’t recruited them, and a blue dot means they’re a member of your party. Once you’ve met them, you can also teleport to them directly by selecting them on the third tab of the map. Recruitment combines much of what we’ve already talked about in this article. All characters require that you have specific support and Renown levels, which you can see when you select them on the map or by clicking the “Character Info” option when you talk to them. Some recruits will also have additional requirements, like paying them money, retrieving a particular item, or completing a paralogue, side quest, or story chapter. In order to recruit anyone, you first need to give them a gift. Any gift will do for the first one, but after that, you should try to find ones you think they’ll like based on their personal preferences. Doing this will also make it possible to dine with them at the inn, which is how you’ll raise their support level high enough to recruit them. The only support level that matters is the one they have with your current protagonist, so make sure you’re inviting both characters to meals. Recruits have different requirements for each of the protagonists. Someone who needs 10 Renown to be recruited by Cai might only need 4 Renown to be recruited by Dietrich. Meals and gifts are limited each week, so you don’t want to spread yourself too thin by trying to appeal to too many recruits at once. It’s wise to focus on a select few recruits at a time, then move on to new ones once you’re successful. New recruitable characters will continually be added as each storyline progresses, including the leaders of squads you defeat during the Heroic Games. So keep an eye on the map in each chapter to see if there are any new orange dots. And just in case this is the kind of thing you worry about: Recruiting a character with one protagonist will not remove them from the pool for other protagonists. So you don’t have to be concerned about leaving later protagonists with nobody to recruit. There you have it, four things to make sure you get a handle on early in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave. For more coverage of this massive game, check out our review , recruitment guide , and 18 things the game doesn’t tell you . Article authored by IGN Global and presented by Charles Schwab. items.title: MTG’s Hobbit Cards Are the Closest Thing to Owning Rare Tolkien Memorabilia, and Perfect for Collectors
items.excerpt: Here's why Magic: The Gathering’s small-ish Hobbit set somehow surpasses the massive Lord of the Rings crossover for die-hard Tolkien collectors, just one month after its release.
items.content_text: For the second time, and likely the last, Magic: The Gathering has taken players back to Middle-Earth with its The Hobbit set (its fifth of the year, if you can believe it), and it’s been pretty great. That’s perhaps to be expected since the original book laid out a lot of what we consider fantasy tropes. Dragons, goblins, dwarves, and more are represented here in a smaller set than the Lord of the Rings one, all of which have gone on to inspire Magic cards in their own right. Still, given how tricky it can be to get some products, there’s a good chance that finding Hobbit items can feel like searching for the Arkenstone in Smaug’s treasure hoard. And yet, it feels like, in a way, that’s kind of the point. Tolkien Collectors Will Love The Hobbit Set J.R.R. Tolkien’s influence on the world of fantasy cannot be overstated, and there’s a reason that so many early editions of his works have fetched colossal sums of money. As an example, back in 2025, a fully signed Lord of the Rings first-edition set sold for around £287,700 (or $337,000). That marks the high point of spending, but it’s not an outlier by any stretch. An unsigned first edition of the book also sold in 2025 for $250,000, while a collection of manuscripts from the author that includes notes written in Elvish has sold for over $200,000, too. Naturally, memorabilia sells big, too, notably from Peter Jackson’s iconic movies. Props, costumes, and limited-edition art prints fetch piles of gold to make a covetous dragon blush, and that includes pieces from The Hobbit movies, too. Of course, those figures are colossal compared to the price of even the most expensive cards in The Hobbit set , but there’s crossover there, too. Whereas the Lord of the Rings set offered full art cards with a slick border treatment that highlighted the series’ characters across heroes and villains, The Hobbit leans into the series’ literary origins with book cover-inspired designs that carry a “well-read” look that makes them feel unique amongst Magic’s wide-ranging treatment offerings. This writer was lucky enough to pack Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane and Smaug, Wicked Worm in the treatment, and they’ve almost instantly become two of my favorite Magic cards I own. There’s just something about the way they look textured that makes them feel like the latest in a long line of Tolkien memorabilia. In fact, I’d go so far as to say that these are my favorite treatments we’ve received in years - and an ideal inclusion for any serious collector. That doesn’t make it any easier to find the cards, mind…

items.title: Disney+ Shows and Movies Are Now Headed to Netflix, Including Ice Age and Percy Jackson
items.excerpt: Disney plans to license a mix of legacy titles and currently-streaming TV shows to Netflix as part of a new deal between the two firms. In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney content for its 325 million subscribers.
items.content_text: Disney plans to license Ice Age, Percy Jackson and more to Netflix as part of a new deal between the two firms. In the deal, Netflix will host select Disney+ content for its 325 million subscribers, including a mix of legacy titles and currently streaming TV shows. The deal is designed to help boost interest in contemporary Disney series such as Percy Jackson and the Olympians, which joins Netflix on October 4. The first two seasons will appear on the rival streaming platform ahead of its Disney+ Season 3 premiere on November 20. All five 20th Century Studios’ Ice Age movies will land on Netflix at the same time as Percy Jackson. Will Trent Seasons 1-4, Shifting Gears Seasons 1-2, and Tracker Seasons 1-3 are also heading to Netflix between November this year and February 2027. In 2027, a range of Walt Disney Animation and Pixar movies will also head to Netflix, including Soul, Elio, and Raya and the Last Dragon, along with a selection of complete series such as Felicity, This is Us, Revenge, and Fresh off the Boat. Release dates for these vary by region. According to the Variety exclusive, this will be a mutually beneficial deal, with Netflix getting more content and Disney getting more eyes on the kind of things it offers outside of its biggest franchise titles (and presumably some cash). Those franchise titles such as Marvel and Star Wars will remain exclusive to Disney+, keeping its Disney-branded titles as the main selling point of the subscription service. Netflix will also continue to invest in its own content, with original series and animations such as Arcane, The Witcher, and Castlevania keeping subscribers fed. Netflix recently announced its streaming lineup for October , which includes miniseries East of Eden, Ben Affleck’s Animals, and Josh Hartnett squaring off against a sea beast in Below. Disney+ has an exciting October coming up too, featuring Marvel’s VisionQuest, horrible (in a good way) horror movie Barbarian, and American Horror Story: 13. With Disney+ and Hulu merging their libraries , there’s more choice than ever over there. It’s just a shame Disney+ had to increase its pricing again ahead of the next big Marvel drop. It’s a bit of a Thor point. If you can’t afford subscriptions to Netflix and Disney, though, at least you’ll be able to catch some Disney+ stuff on Netflix from October 4.

items.title: James Gunn's DCU Reportedly Safe Following Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger, for Now at Least
items.excerpt: DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will seemingly keep their vision for the DCU alive following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger.
items.content_text: UPDATE October 2, 2026, 12:22 p.m. PT: Skydance's David Ellison reportedly told James Gunn and Peter Safran to "keep doing what you're doing" at a meeting that took place earlier this week. The Hollywood Reporter 's sources say the two moviemakers are staying right where they are "at least for the foreseeable future" after they had a positive meeting with Ellison yesterday. They were both invited to stay, with one source saying that Ellison asked them to simply "keep doing what you're doing." He also allegedly visited the Man of Tomorrow set in Atlanta earlier this summer. Who the two DC Studios CEOs will report to in the immediate future, however, is less clear. Deadline also corroborated reports that Gunn and Safran will continue to build out their DCU as the merger is finalized. ORIGINAL STORY: DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran will seemingly keep their vision for the DCU alive following the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger. Rumors that the two comic book movie executives would be shuffled out amidst the tumultuous merger have swirled for months. Now, as the $110 billion deal comes to a close under its new Skydance banner , it seems Gunn and Safran – as well as the cinematic universe that includes projects like 2025's Superman and Lanterns – are safe. Puck has reported that both creatives "will be invited to stay on at DC, at least initially" as all the moving pieces come together behind the scenes. What the long-term future holds remains to be seen, but it sounds like more DC movies and shows will continue to fall in line as the DCU navigates its early ups and downs. Adding weight to the continuation of the current iteration of the DC universe is Gunn himself. After that new Skydance title was announced, the former Marvel director took to Instagram to celebrate the news by sharing its flashy new trailer. Included amongst the cuts of Paramount and Warner Bros. logos are shots from Superman, Robert Pattinson's The Batman, and even the DC logo itself. "What once was the peak, is now just the beginning," Gunn, echoing the trailer, said in the post's caption. Gunn and Safran officially took over the DC entertainment business in 2022 and will continue to oversee it – at least through 2027. That's when their contracts are set to expire, and while there are plenty of other projects set to release before then, whether they'll choose to renew under new leadership remains to be seen. In the meantime, the DCU charges ahead. After Superman started things off with a bang and Supergirl failed to live up expectations , the cinematic universe is just days away from airing the Lanterns Season 1 finale . The Green Lantern introduction series has received praise from critics and fans thanks to strong casting choices in Kyle Chandler as Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre as John Stewart. Next up for this month is a theatrical release in Batman body horror spinoff, Clayface . items.title: Brand New GTA 6 Screenshots Focus on Lucia and Jason's Relationship
items.excerpt: Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.
items.content_text: Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason. GTA 6's dynamic criminal duo can be seen in four new images published via Love Magazine , which features an illustration of the couple on its cover, and a black-and-white screenshot of the pair in more casual clothes (Jason in a white vest, jacked arms on show, Lucia in a leopard-print crop top). Two more images show Lucia and Jason together in the booth of a diner, but sat opposite. Is this the setting of a heist planning session, or are the two about to hold-up the very diner they're sat in? Are they having a date, or an argument about the way their criminal undertakings are going? What looks like a large bag set to be filled with stolen money suggests something is afoot. Next up are images of Lucia and Jason in more stylish clothes (well, Jason is in bike leathers), and looking fierce while playing pool in what appears to be a biker bar. The article also includes further detail from Rockstar senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, who discussed the pair's pursuit of the American Dream. GTA 6 portrays this as the couple seeking the ability to own a house and pay off their various debts, rather than a desire to become billionaires. “If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face,” Humphries said. “Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world.” "We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other,” game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern told Love. “That’s what we felt made them authentic, and a great team.” Game writer Alexa D’Agostino added: “When you are focusing on writing a fully realised person with their own wants, you’re going to get something perfectly imperfect — with clichés, but also undeniably real.” Speaking of GTA 6 marketing ramping up, The Miami Heat announced it would be heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks . The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an "all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court." We've got extensive coverage of GTA 6 across IGN. Check out IGN's interview with Rockstar Games , our GTA 6 preview , and word of the first confirmed GTA 6 voice actor .
